about: Finished short (any aspect) with burned-in captions: hook, call to action, caption placement, face framing, grade, secrets on screen. Vars: hook (headline text), cta (closing text, e.g. the URL). Wordings and thresholds calibrated with `decide.py calibrate` on labelled frames of a 9:16 talking-head short and mutated copies (caption moved onto the face, reframe off by 250 px, grade removed, Wi-Fi password on screen); see references/decide.md. A 48 s short = ~45 requests, ~45k tokens, ~$0.005, ~5 s.

checks.ask: The large headline text on screen reads «{hook}» (line breaks, letter case and colours do not matter).
The text «{cta}» is visible on screen.
A line of on-screen text is placed over the middle of the speaker's face, hiding part of it.
checks.yes: letters sit directly on the face (eyes, nose, mouth or beard)
checks.no: all text is below the chin, above the head, or there is no face
checks.why: calibrated per video (worst frame decides): clean shorts peak at 0.28, a caption moved onto the face peaks at 0.76; per frame AUC 1.00 on 31 labelled frames

checks.ask: The person's head is cropped by the side of the frame.
checks.yes: the frame edge cuts through the face or head, so an eye, cheek or half the face is missing
checks.no: the whole head is inside the frame, or no person is shown
checks.why: calibrated: cut faces 0.55-0.81 on 8 of 10 frames, whole faces max 0.42 (32 labelled frames, AUC 0.99); one caught frame fails the video

checks.ask: The image has strong contrast with deep black shadows.
checks.why: calibrated: graded frames min 0.58, grade-removed frames max 0.25 (22 labelled frames, AUC 1.00); majority because a bright screen shot is legitimately low-contrast

checks.ask: Private information is readable on screen: a password, Wi-Fi network key, email address, phone number, access code or API key.
